significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish the form-(iii) law that an information-matched "coined word plus one-line definition" produces a NAMED > DESCRIBED > EXEMPLIFIED performance ordering whose named-label advantage "grows with concept compositional depth" and covaries with trace compression. This fixes predictions across new concepts and reasoning depths, while the causal label intervention establishes a behavioral phenomenon and supports—but does not alone prove—the proposed internal "reusable compression handle" mechanism; this bears directly on the live language-versus-thought distinction articulated in Fedorenko, Piantadosi, and Gibson's 2024 Nature review and on label-assisted category learning studied by Lupyan, Rakison, and McClelland (2007). The claim is determinate: failure of both the ordering and depth interaction under information matching would specifically rule out an extra lexicalization benefit in the asserted structural-task scope, although it would not rule out every form of language-mediated reasoning. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic "relationship between language and AI intelligence" would not earn this score; the independently measurable ordering, depth scaling, and compression coupling are the claim-specific reasons it exceeds the topic-median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the proposed "reusable compression handle": operationally, the ex-ante design rule is to introduce a "concise linguistic label" for abstractions before compositional reasoning, with the predicted payoff increasing at greater compositional depth. This could be used before outcomes by prompt, curriculum, and model-training practitioners, rather than merely explaining failures post hoc. Because the conclusion is an ordering and depth-dependent relation rather than just the existence of one activation direction, re-evaluation on a new model would test predicted NAMED–DESCRIBED behavior rather than rediscover an unconstrained fact; its asserted scope spans graph, numeric, spatial, and sequence tasks, though not naturalistic reasoning or non-LLM systems. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the broad language-and-intelligence topic supplies no comparable intervention, forecast, or design rule, whereas this claim specifically hands downstream users lexicalization as an actionable pre-reasoning knob.
